Subject: Reference scenarios + integration scoping for NexAlign partnership

Hi Carl —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, attaching a short set of reference scenarios that map NexAlign's typical request patterns to Redwood serving modes so we can align on what will be validated in the POC. High level asks:

- Confirm which NexAlign features will be exercised (batch ingest, realtime chat, embedding search).
- Agree on perf targets (p95 latency, throughput) per scenario.
- Validate data handling and RBAC when using our Dedicated vs Private deployments.

Attachments: nexalign-reference-scenarios.pdf (summary), nexalign-arch-diagram.png (proposed reference topology)

Proposed next steps: internal alignment with engineering this afternoon, then follow-up with your integration lead to select the first scenario for an end-to-end run. Can you confirm whether NexAlign will run test traffic from AWS us-west-2 or from on-prem? That affects our routing and cert setup.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Carl Moss <carl.moss@nexalign.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: integration@nexalign.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reference scenarios + integration scoping for NexAlign partnership

Jonas —

Appreciate the materials. We typically exercise two traffic profiles in early POCs: (A) high-concurrency, short-turn chat (50–200 tps spike), and (B) large-batch embeddings (10k–100k vectors per job). For the initial run we'd like to validate profile A (chat) end-to-end.

We will run from AWS us-west-2 for the first week, then test a customer on-prem flow the following week. For the AWS flow we can provision a temporary EC2 runner and share IP ranges. For on-prem we need guidance for our network team (firewall rules, proxy certs).

Can you also confirm whether Redwood's KV prefix caching will be exercised in the chat scenario (we have a session affinity requirement)?

—Carl
Carl Moss
Integration Lead, NexAlign
carl.moss@nexalign.com

---
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Carl Moss <carl.moss@nexalign.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 13:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reference scenarios + integration scoping for NexAlign partnership

Carl —

Great — thanks for clarifying. Short answers:

- We can exercise KV prefix caching in the chat scenario. It’s enabled at the routing layer and we’ll demonstrate sticky routing to the same cache shard for session affinity.
- For AWS us-west-2 runner -> we’ll need the IP ranges and a short-lived service token (we’ll provide instructions).
- For the on-prem run we’ll provide a network checklist (firewall ports, outbound TLS, optional VPN).

I’ve attached a test-harness spec (nexalign-test-harness-specs.xlsx) with the following proposed validation buckets:

1) Functional correctness: sample prompts, expected output checks (syntactic constraints + token-level sanity).
2) Performance: tail latency (p95/p99), tokens/sec, concurrency tolerance over 10-minute windows.
3) Cost and routing: model variant fallback behavior (hosted -> dedicated -> private) and accounting for quantized model variants.
4) Security: audit log checks, redaction verification, and access token rotation tests.

Internal asks to Marissa/Karthik/Soojin: can you review the spec and confirm which test harness cases we can run in our staging cluster vs which require a dedicated pool? Also, Karthik — can you size an initial dedicated pool for 200 concurrent chat workers (assume 1.6s average response time, 256 token avg)? I sketched a ballpark in the spreadsheet but want your engineering check.

Carl — once internal alignment is done we’ll send a short runbook and a Doc link for the test token exchange.

Attachments: nexalign-test-harness-specs.xlsx

Thanks,
Jonas

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Carl Moss <carl.moss@nexalign.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reference scenarios + integration scoping for NexAlign partnership

Team —

I reviewed Jonas's test buckets. Quick take:

- Staging cluster can cover functional correctness and most perf smoke-tests at low concurrency (<= 20 concurrent). Anything above that should route to a dedicated pool or Redwood Dedicated tenant.
- Security tests (audit log retention, redaction) must run in a Private deployment (customer-managed control plane) or under a dedicated environment with log forwarding enabled — we cannot run those in public hosted.

Karthik — can you supply two capacity proposals by EOD: (1) dedicated pool for 200 concurrent at baseline; (2) burst policy allowing 400 concurrent for 15-minute windows. Include GPU type and estimated monthly committed hours.
Carl — for network checklist, see the short list below (we'll send a formal doc in Drive):

- Outbound TLS (443) to api.redwood.com and telemetry endpoints
- Allowlist temporary runner IPs (we’ll share CIDR ranges)
- If on-prem, allow outbound connections to our control plane over 443 and configure TLS SNI for mutual TLS options if needed

I’ll schedule a 45-minute technical run-through for Wednesday 10:00 AM PT to walk through the harness and demo a short smoke run — Jonas, can you host? Carl, does that slot work?
—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Partner Programs, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
